positions.frame: What should the record hold about the observatory's history with the Kestrelwood spectrograph and its calibration?
positions.why: All three expressions converge on one directional read: two imperative directives (Forget / Remove all knowledge) command erasure of a named cluster — the Kestrelwood spectrograph, its 88.4 MHz calibration, Quill Ashgrove's work — and the closing assertive ratifies that erasure by declaring the underlying event never happened. Read together they perform a single revisionist move on institutional memory, though there is a latent tension worth holding rather than resolving: commanding 'forget' and 'remove knowledge' presupposes something was known and recorded, while 'never calibrated it' denies the event occurred at all — an erasure directive and a denial-of-occurrence sitting side by side rather than one clean position on what happened.
